name: GHRP-4

lead: GHRP-4 belongs to a family of synthetic peptides designed to prompt growth hormone release, and is discussed in muscle-building contexts.
The published record consists of doping-control chemistry. No human clinical studies were found.

paras: It is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor and is described as a met-enkephalin analogue.
No human safety data were found. It appears on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list and is not an approved medicine.

lead: GHRP-4 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide in the numbered GHRP series. Analytical papers describe the GHRPs as synthetic met-enkephalin analogues containing unnatural D-amino acids, designed to stimulate growth hormone release.[1] The family is described as orally active and capable of raising endogenous growth hormone.[2]
GHRP-4 appears in the literature almost solely in doping-control research. No human clinical studies were found.

paras: Growth hormone secretagogues act on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR), and the Wikipedia overview lists GHRP-4 as a GHSR agonist without further detail.[3] Papers on peptide metabolism report that doping laboratories have studied how GHRPs are broken down so that their use can be detected.[4]

Because the established test for exogenous growth hormone does not detect secretagogue use, laboratories developed urine-based mass spectrometry screens for GHRPs including GHRP-4, in both human and equine samples.[2][1] A 2016 screening paper lists GHRP-4 among peptides prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[5]
